title: Parcel shipping fee by zone and weight
description: A carrier prices parcels by zone and weight. Write parcel_fee, which takes a zone name and a weight in grams and returns the fee in cents. The zones are "local", "national" and "international" (lower case, compared exactly). Each zone has a base fee that covers the first started kilogram, a surcharge for every further started kilogram, and a weight limit: local costs 300 base plus 50 per further kilogram with a limit of 30000 grams; national costs 500 plus 100 with a limit of 30000 grams; international costs 1500 plus 400 with a limit of 20000 grams. A started kilogram is a kilogram that has begun, so 1000 grams is one kilogram and 1001 grams is two. A weight equal to the limit is allowed. Checks happen in this order, and the first failing one decides the result: a weight of zero or less gives the error "invalid weight"; a zone that is not one of the three names gives "unknown zone: " followed by the zone text; a weight above the zone's limit gives "too heavy for " followed by the zone, then ": limit is ", the limit and " g" (for example "too heavy for international: limit is 20000 g").

args: too heavy for international: limit is 20000 g

notes: Level 1: lookup by name, ceiling division on positive numbers, three ordered checks. Pitfalls: the weight check precedes the zone check (a bad weight with an unknown zone is a weight error); exactly 1000 g has no surcharge; the limit itself is allowed; the limit differs for international.
